Devon Air Ambulance sends helicopters and rapid-response cars (together, HEMS: helicopter emergency medical service) to the most serious emergency calls. This project simulates that service day by day so you can ask "what if" questions, such as "what if a second helicopter flew 24 hours a day?", and see how many calls would go unattended.

**DAA_DES** is a *discrete event simulation* built on **SimPy** and packaged as `air_ambulance_des`, with a **Streamlit web app** in `app/` for setting parameters, running the model and viewing results. Each simulation run generates daily emergency calls, samples patient characteristics from *distributions fitted to historical job data*, tries to allocate a helicopter or car according to rotas, servicing schedules and *care category* priorities, and records every step in an **event log**. Many seeded **replications** run in parallel, and the combined results are summarised and set against **historical data** so that scenarios can be compared with current performance.

**Source repository:** <https://github.com/RichardPilbery/DAA_DES>

## Choose your version

The two technical versions cover the same eight parts of the system, in the same order, and differ in depth. The two no-code versions are organised around questions: those of someone deciding whether to rely on the model, and those of a domain expert checking that it reflects how the service really works.

[Intermediate](intermediate/index.qmd){.btn .btn-primary} Comfortable with Python, new to this codebase.

[Contributor](advanced-contributor/index.qmd){.btn .btn-outline-primary} An experienced engineer about to change this codebase: internals, invariants, extension points, sharp edges and design rationale.

[Decision-makers](stakeholder-decision-maker/index.qmd){.btn .btn-outline-primary} Managers and funders deciding whether to rely on the model. No code: what it does, what it assumes, the risks, and what to ask the team.

[Domain experts](stakeholder-domain-expert/index.qmd){.btn .btn-outline-primary} Clinicians, operational managers and analysts who must sanity-check the model. No code: the rules and values it applies, how to read its results, and where it differs from reality.
